newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares overcome rate woes, post gains.
newsitem.headline: German shares overcome rate woes, post gains.

text.p: German shares posted modest gains on Wednesday, as fears that the Bundesbank is poised to hike German interest rates in the near future ebbed.

The blue-chip DAX index climbed 32.71 points, or 0.8 percent, to 4,335.39 points, clocking up the bulk of gains just before the session close as the dollar briefly rose above an eight-year high of 1.89 marks.
In late trade the IBIS DAX extended its gains on the back of early Wall Street gains to end the day up 4,364.25 points.

The dollar was a trigger for most of the day, first buoying share prices as it strengthened against the mark during bourse trade and then giving the market new grounds for optimism as it pared those gains in the afternoon.

The dollar has become a double-edged indicator for German shares. A very strong U.S. currency enhances prospects for German exporters. However, when it weakens slightly, the dollar reduces the risk that the Bundesbank may be forced to act to support the deutschemark.
Supporting the case against a rate rise earlier in the day was data showing the German seasonally-adjusted unemployment total had risen by a stronger than expected 17,000 in July.
Isolated big-ticket shares, such as Siemens which rose 2.50 marks to 123.80 marks in bourse trade on healthy volumes, carried the market higher.
Sportswear manufacturer Adidas got an early boost after it reported that its first-half profit jumped to 238 million marks from 184 million marks -- at the top end of forecasts.
The shares hit a high of 223 marks in IBIS trade before settling back to end bourse at 218 marks, up two marks.
